tool_input.content:
---
name: batch-ai-analysis
description: Background batch AI word-analysis feature — architecture, cache keying, and two non-obvious gotchas.
metadata:
  type: project
---

Batch AI word-analysis (added 2026-06-21) runs the existing per-word analysis over all saved vocabulary in the background.

- **Engine:** `Models/BatchExplanationController.swift` — `@Observable @MainActor` singleton (like every store), owns an unstructured `Task` + a `withTaskGroup` sliding window of size `AIModelSettings.batchConcurrency` (1…10, default 3). Progress/cancel state is on the singleton, so it survives view teardown and any view observing it shows live progress (the requirement: navigate away from Settings and back, bar still live). UI: `Views/Components/BatchAIAnalysisView.swift` (`BatchAIAnalysisControls` returns Sections, embedded in iOS `MoreView` push + macOS `AISettingsTab`; `BatchAIAnalysisStatusBadge` is the live MoreView-row badge).
- **"Unprocessed" = cache miss:** a term is analyzed iff `WordExplanationCacheStore.hasExplanation(forWord: term.headlineText, directionToken:)` is false. Batch must store under `term.headlineText` + `directionToken` (NOT `term.chinese`) so the detail view's `AIWordExplanationView` finds it. See [[ai-provider-architecture]].
- **Import/export AI analysis:** `VocabularyImportExportService` — JSON uses a versioned `ExportEnvelope` (schemaVersion 2, lossless `aiExplanations`), tried before the legacy `[SavedTerm]` array on import. CSV appends `AI Definition`/`AI Examples` (human) + `AI Data` (base64 of compact JSON `[CachedWordExplanation]`, CSV-safe). `includeAIAnalysis` toggle in both export UIs; restore via `WordExplanationCacheStore.merge`.

**Gotcha 1 (real parallelism):** `AIWordExplanationService`/`CloudAIService`/`OllamaService` are all `@MainActor`, but they suspend at `await session.data(...)`, releasing the main actor during network I/O — so N concurrent child tasks genuinely overlap on the network. `@MainActor` only serializes the fast synchronous parts.

**Gotcha 2 (CSV CRLF):** Swift coalesces `\r\n` into a SINGLE `Character` grapheme, so a char-by-char `c == "\n" || c == "\r"` split MISSES CRLF and treats a Windows/Excel CSV as one giant record. Use `Character.isNewline` (matches `\n`, `\r`, and the `\r\n` grapheme). `components(separatedBy: .newlines)` is scalar-based and avoids this, but can't do quote-aware splitting.

While a batch run is in progress, BatchAIAnalysisControls recomputed the
unprocessed-word count on every render (and ~4× per render across its
subviews), and each computation scanned the whole explanation cache calling
normalizedKey() per entry — O(terms × entries) with string allocations. The
view re-renders on every store and every progress tick, so the main thread

  hasExplanation() now does a set lookup instead of a full O(n) scan. The
  index is observed, so the live "remaining" count still updates.
- BatchAIAnalysisControls: compute the unprocessed count once per render and
  thread it through overviewSection/actionSection/startButton instead of
  recomputing it in each.
